# Product Requirements Document: 485

**Version:** 1.0.0  
**Created:** 2026-02-18

## 1. Overview

Project 485 requirements and specifications.

## 2. Objectives

- \*Launch functional e-commerce platform\*\* by Q2 2025
- \*Migrate 50% of sales\*\* from marketplaces to owned platform by Q4 2025
- \*Build customer database\*\* of 50,000 registered users in first year
- \*Achieve profitability\*\* on direct sales by Q3 2025
- generated content
- driven product recommendation engine
- Goals (Out of Scope for V1)
- International shipping (US-only initially)
- Subscription/membership programs
- Mobile native apps (mobile web only)

## 3. Success Metrics

- \*Technical Readiness\*\*:
- ✅ All 10 providers pass smoke tests
- ✅ End-to-end deployment successful on all providers
- ✅ Rollback tested and working
- ✅ Security audit passed
- ✅ Performance benchmarks met
- \*Documentation Readiness\*\*:
- ✅ API documentation 100% complete
- ✅ User guides for all providers
- ✅ Migration guide from AWS-only

````bash
### FR-1175: Consistency

Ensure all projects follow the same structure

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |

- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |

- *Use when**:

- YYY: Story 2

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

### FR-1177: Speed

Start with 80% of the structure already done

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- Project has < 20 distinct tasks

- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints

- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- Project has < 20 distinct tasks

- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2

- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |

- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed

- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence

- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points

- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:

- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

### FR-1204: Using PERT Template



**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- Measures **risk** through variance calculations

- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

### FR-1217: 3. Scale Templates as Project Grows



**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- XXX: Story 1

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6

- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

**Acceptance Criteria:**

- Project has < 20 distinct tasks

- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints

- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence

- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points

- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence

- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- *Waterfall** | Detailed or Enterprise | Waterfall |
- *Kanban** | Simple | Simple |
- *Hybrid** | Detailed | Simple or Waterfall |
- *Startups**:
- Use: Simple templates
- Why: Speed over process, rapid iteration
- Focus: Just enough planning to execute
- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams
- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management
- *Recommended Combinations**:
- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |
- ✓ Using template > 3 times with same modifications
- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects
- ✗ One-off projects
- ✗ Learning/experimentation
- ✗ Already-well-served by existing templates

Best case if everything goes right


### FR-1242: Most Likely (M)

Realistic estimate under normal conditions


### FR-1243: Pessimistic (P)

Worst case if everything goes wrong


### FR-1244: > 90%

Very likely, low risk


### FR-1245: 70-90%

Likely, moderate risk


### FR-1246: 50-70%

Uncertain, higher risk


### FR-1247: < 50%

Unlikely, high risk

Earliest a task can start (max EF of predecessors)

ES + Expected Duration


### FR-1250: LF

Latest a task can finish without delaying project

LF - Expected Duration

### FR-1682: 70-90%

Likely, moderate risk

Uncertain, higher risk

Unlikely, high risk

ES + Expected Duration

LF - Expected Duration
````

````bash
## 7. Non-Functional Requirements

### NFR-1: Security notes

- Child processes are spawned with `shell: false` to avoid shell injection and quoting issues.
- Inputs are validated with Zod; unknown types are rejected.
- Avoid logging secrets; DEBUG only prints argv and minimal env context.

### NFR-2: Performance

- **Plan Generation:** <2 min for 2-3K lines (275x faster)
- **Execution:** 2.75x parallel speedup (91.7% efficiency)
- **Memory:** 75% reduction with batching
- **Overhead:** 3ms total (500x better than target)
- **Cost:** 99.95% cheaper than manual

---

### NFR-3: Performance Targets

| Metric | Target |
| :--- | :--- |
| Agent Startup | < 2ms |
| Human Startup | < 40ms |
| Input Latency | < 5ms (Asynchronous) |
| Completion UI | Instant (fzf-tab cached) |

### 🟡 Create GitHub Issues from WBS Tasks

Automatically create issues with proper metadata, labels, and estimates

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- -----------|--------------|--------------|
- *Mark as Completed:**
- `fixes #TASK_ID`
- `closes #TASK_ID`
- `resolves #TASK_ID`
- `completes #TASK_ID`
- *Mark as In Progress:**
- `in progress on #TASK_ID`
- `working on #TASK_ID`
- `started #TASK_ID`
- `wip #TASK_ID`
- *Examples:**
- m "fixes #1.1 - authentication working"
- m "in progress on #2.3 and #2.4"
- *Set Status:**
- *Set Progress:**
- -repo owner/repo`
- -repo owner/repo`
- create_issue: 2
- update_issue: 3
- Issue #123 has no task ID - cannot sync
- *Resolution:**
- *Task ID:** `1.1``
- run sync
- `wbs-task` - Identifies WBS-synchronized issues
- `status: *` - Task status labels
- `priority: *` - Priority labels
- if one fails, others continue.
- *Fix:** Set valid token in environment or `.env` file

### 🟡 Total Work

Sum of PERT expected estimates for all leaf tasks


### 🟡 Ideal Line

Linear progression from total work to zero


### 🟡 Actual Progress

Based on task completion status


### 🟡 Velocity

Work completed per day (hours/day)


### 🟡 Predicted Completion

Forecast based on current velocity


### 🟡 PV (Planned Value)

Budget × Planned % Complete (should have done)


### 🟡 EV (Earned Value)

Budget × Actual % Complete (actually done)


### 🟡 AC (Actual Cost)

Sum of actual costs (actually spent)


### 🟡 SV (Schedule Variance)

EV - PV


### 🟡 CV (Cost Variance)

EV - AC


### 🟡 SPI (Schedule Performance Index)

EV / PV


### 🟡 CPI (Cost Performance Index)

EV / AC


### 🟡 EAC (Estimate at Completion)

BAC / CPI


### 🟡 ETC (Estimate to Complete)

EAC - AC


### 🟡 VAC (Variance at Completion)

BAC - EAC

PV should reflect achievable targets


### 🟡 Track actual costs

More accurate AC = better forecasts


### 🟡 Review regularly

Weekly variance review catches issues early


### 🟡 Act on trends

Consistently low SPI/CPI requires intervention


### 🟡 Update forecasts

Adjust EAC when performance changes significantly


### 🟡 Review risks weekly

Risk status changes over time


### 🟡 Implement mitigations

Don't just identify, take action


### 🟡 Track to closure

Monitor risks until fully mitigated


### 🟡 Update probabilities

Adjust as project progresses


### 🟡 Add new risks

Continuously identify emerging risks


### 🟡 Share widely

Stakeholders need visibility


### 🟡 Update weekly

Fresh data drives better decisions


### 🟡 Follow up on actions

Recommendations only work if implemented


### 🟡 Track trends

Health declining over time is a warning sign


### 🟡 Be honest

Accurate reporting is better than optimistic reporting

Ensure all projects follow the same structure

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

### 🟡 [PERT Documentation](../pert/README.md)

- PERT scheduling

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |

- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- path project.yaml

- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |

- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed

- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points

- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task

- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation

- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

### 🟡 What is PERT?



**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

### 🟡 WBS Validation



**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

### 🟡 5. When to Customize Templates



**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- path project.yaml

- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- *Startups**:
- Use: Simple templates
- Why: Speed over process, rapid iteration

- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure

- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management

- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |

- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects

- ✗ Learning/experimentation
- ✗ Already-well-served by existing templates

### 🟡 Template as Safety Net



**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |

- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points

- Each phase must complete before next

- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation

- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

Best case if everything goes right


### 🟡 Most Likely (M)

Realistic estimate under normal conditions


### 🟡 Pessimistic (P)

Worst case if everything goes wrong


### 🟡 > 90%

Very likely, low risk


### 🟡 70-90%

Likely, moderate risk


### 🟡 50-70%

Uncertain, higher risk


### 🟠 < 50%

Unlikely, high risk


### 🟡 ES

Earliest a task can start (max EF of predecessors)


### 🟡 EF

ES + Expected Duration


### 🟡 LF

Latest a task can finish without delaying project


### 🟡 LS

LF - Expected Duration

### 🟡 Optimistic (O)

Best case if everything goes right


### 🟡 Most Likely (M)

Realistic estimate under normal conditions


### 🟡 Pessimistic (P)

Worst case if everything goes wrong


### 🟡 > 90%

Very likely, low risk


### 🟡 70-90%

Likely, moderate risk


### 🟡 50-70%

Uncertain, higher risk


### 🟠 < 50%

Unlikely, high risk


### 🟡 ES

Earliest a task can start (max EF of predecessors)


### 🟡 EF

ES + Expected Duration


### 🟡 LF

Latest a task can finish without delaying project


### 🟡 LS

LF - Expected Duration
````

````bash
### System Design

````

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ BytePort CLI │
│ (Go) - NVMS Parser, Config Validator, Deployment Orchestrator │
└────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│
▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ CloudProvider Interface │
│ (Go Interface - provider abstraction layer) │
└────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────┬────────┘
│ │
▼ ▼
┌────────────────────────────┐ ┌────────────────────────────────┐
│ Go Providers │ │ Python Providers │
│ │ │ │
│ ┌──────────────┐ │ │ ┌───

```
### Cost Estimation

Assuming average loaded cost of $200/hour ($1600/day, $8000/week):

**Phase 0** (60 pw): $480,000
**Phase 1** (200 pw): $1,600,000
**Phase 2** (150 pw): $1,200,000
**Phase 3** (80 pw): $640,000

**Total Project Cost**: ~$3,920,000 (6 months, 12-15 engineers)

**Infrastructure Costs** (AWS/GCP):
- Gateway servers: $3,000-5,000/month
- Database (PostgreSQL RDS): $1,000-2,000/month
- Cache (ElastiCache): $500-1,000/month
- Monitoring (Datadog/New Relic): $2,000-3,000/month
- CDN for installer distribution: $500-1,000/month

**Monthly Infrastructure**: $7,000-12,000/month
**6-Month Infrastructure**: $42,000-72,000

**Total 6-Month Investment**: $3,960,000 - $3,990,000
```
